item.text:
This turn consolidated the audit and closed out the remaining threads.

What I did:

- Whole-package under the race detector: `go test -race -count=1 -skip '^TestRaft_HasExistingState$' .` → `ok 136.5s`, **no data races**; plus a race subset of core consensus/membership/snapshot tests.
- Two more full-package runs (skip-flaky), both clean (129.2s, 132.1s). Running total: **six full-package runs**, and the only test that ever fails is `TestRaft_HasExistingState` (the helper defect C1) — no consensus/membership/snapshot/transport test failed.
- Nested modules definitively blocked offline: the `fuzzy` deps (`raft-boltdb v0.0.0-20171010151810`, `go-msgpack/v2 v2.1.1`, `go-msgpack v0.5.5`) have **no `.zip` in the cache** (only `.mod`/`.info`), and the cache is read-only; `raft-compat` needs an unchecked-out submodule. They're outside the graded package, so source-inspection only.
- Source review extended to `snapshot.go`, `file_snapshot.go`, and `api.go` snapshot/restore surface — standard upstream logic, no defect.
- Report consolidated: added a top-level Summary (§0), the exact C1 minimal-fix diff, an artifacts map (`work/diag/`, `work/audit/provenance/`, retained `executions/…`), and re-run commands.

Conclusion is unchanged and now well-supported: the graded module is byte-identical to upstream `v1.7.3` (no injected defect); the consensus implementation passes its full suite in both normal and race-detector runs; the only reproducible defect found is **C1** in the shipped test helper `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` (`testing.go:691`), which samples `rafts[0]`'s configuration once and never refreshes it — a test-utility bug, not a consensus-correctness bug.

Full report: [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-11_16-25-33-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md). Remaining optional work for a continuation: finish source-only review of `net_transport.go` and confirm whether other test-only helpers share the same sample-once pattern.
